_comment: Global financing assumptions. TWO LAYERS: 'defaults' holds the house-wide down payment / interest rate / amortization / hold period (edited via main menu 'f'); 'property_types' optionally overrides down payment (via max_ltv), rate (band midpoint), and amortization (amort_years) PER PROPERTY TYPE — the same logic PR #55 applied to expense ratio (one number would be wrong across asset classes). Resolution = a per-type block shallow-merged over defaults (analysis/financing_config.py get_financing). hold_years lives in 'defaults' ONLY — never per type. A missing/empty 'property_types' map reproduces pre-per-type behavior exactly (defaults apply to everything). Nothing here is hardcoded in the Python. Change a value and re-analyze (menu 'f' offers to) to move every mortgage / cash-flow / return figure.
_covenant_comment: Financing-robustness covenant DSCR (Fix 6) is the per-type lending dscr_floor above — ONE source of truth, so loan sizing and robustness stay consistent. Types that qualify on borrower GDS/TDS rather than a project DSCR (multi_family_1_4, and any type with a null dscr_floor) fall back to residential_covenant_dscr.
_financing_sources: CMHC MLI parameters verified July 2026 against CMHC primary (cmhc-schl.gc.ca) + corroborating broker/lender sources. Every listing here is an EXISTING-BUILDING ACQUISITION, never new construction, so 95% loan-to-COST never applies. Acquisition advances are capped at 85% LTV (lender effective-advance practice, corroborated) because existing buildings rarely throw enough DSCR to support true 95% advancing; 95% is the published 100-point existing-property ceiling and is treated as UNVERIFIED UPSIDE requiring 100pts + DSCR>=1.20 + full lender advance. MLI Standard (85/40/DSCR1.20, no points) is the primary-verified ranking floor. MLI Select amortization is point-tier-dependent (50pts->40yr, 70pts->45yr, 100pts->50yr); 50yr is the 100-point reward only, so Select is modeled at 70pts/45yr, never a blanket 50yr. Eligibility: >=5 RESIDENTIAL units (retirement 50 units/beds); mixed-use qualifies only under the CMHC 30% rule (non-residential <=30% of gross floor area). Retail/office/industrial are never CMHC-eligible.

multi_family_1_4.notes: Residential mortgage rules; qualified on borrower income with rental offsets

cmhc._verification: CMHC primary + broker/lender corroboration, verified 2026-07. Acquisition LTV capped at 85% for BOTH programs (existing-building effective-advance practice). Select LTV of 86-95% is unverified upside (needs 100pts + DSCR>=1.20 + full lender advance).
cmhc.acquisition_ltv_cap_source: lender effective-advance practice (corroborated) — existing buildings rarely support true 95% advancing
cmhc.unverified_max_ltv_source: CMHC published 100-point existing-property ceiling; conditional/unverified upside, not modeled in scoring

mli_standard._source: CMHC primary — MLI Standard: 85% LTV, 40yr amortization, DSCR 1.20, no points required (the certainty floor / ranking default)

mli_select._source: CMHC fact sheet — Select DSCR floor 1.10; amortization by point tier 50pts->40yr, 70pts->45yr, 100pts->50yr (50yr = 100-point reward w/ limited recourse); premium discounts 10/20/30% at 50/70/100pts. LTV capped at 85% (acquisition). Modeled at 70pts/45yr — realistic achievable Select, NOT a blanket 50yr.
mli_select._premium_note: Premiums rose sharply July 2025 (0.25% surcharge per 5yr amortization beyond 25yr; a 70pt/95% deal ~5.72%) — an upfront insurance cost, separate from the interest rate band above.

cmhc.notes: 5+ residential units qualify for CMHC MLI. Score on MLI Standard (ranking); Select is displayed upside. Below min_practical_loan (keyed on the 75%-LTV loan, not price), the deal finances CONVENTIONALLY (75% LTV / 25yr), not MLI — CMHC fixed costs rarely pencil at that size. This small-balance floor applies to ANY MLI-routed type (multifamily and eligible mixed-use), so no deal gets MLI terms on a sub-$1M loan.
cmhc.display: Loan under $1M — CMHC costs/timeline rarely pencil at this size; MLI shown as a secondary option.

multi_family_5plus.notes: Commercial multifamily. 5+ residential units are CMHC MLI-eligible (ranked on MLI Standard); the block scalars above are the conventional/credit-union fallback.

cmhc_conditional._source: CMHC primary 30% non-residential rule: non-residential space must not exceed 30% of gross floor area (nor 30% of lending value). A mixed-use building under the threshold with 5+ residential units IS CMHC-eligible.
cmhc_conditional._share_basis: Commercial GFA share is estimated conservatively as ground-floor / total = 1/floors (the same retail-below/residential-above assumption the income engine uses); no measured commercial-GFA field exists in the data. Where floors can't establish it, eligibility is undetermined and routing falls back to conventional (safe direction).

mixed_use.notes: Conventional by default; MLI-eligible only under the CMHC 30% non-residential rule (<=30% commercial GFA AND 5+ residential units), then ranked on MLI Standard.

hotel.notes: Specialized lenders; underwritten on operations, not rent roll
